question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping maintains firm control over the Chinese Communist Party and military as of September 2026, with ongoing anti-corruption purges eliminating potential rivals and leaving the Central Military Commission dominated by loyalists. At age 73, he has shown no signs of stepping aside, deferred succession planning, or internal challenges ahead of the 2027 Party Congress, where analysts expect continuity rather than transition. Traders price the "No" outcome at 95.5% due to the absence of credible mechanisms for early removal in China's centralized system, reinforced by Xi's institutional dominance since abolishing term limits. Realistic shifts before 2027 remain limited to unforeseen events such as acute health developments or sudden elite realignments, though recent patterns indicate these would require exceptional disruption to alter the current trajectory.
